text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx and gateway timeouts detected for private-vpc-transit-gw (inference-gateway-prod) starting ~10:04 UTC. Error spike to 18% 5xx, increased latency. Paging oncall.

oncall-erica: taking. I'm on call, will triage ASAP. Any initial blast radius notes?

prod-monitoring-bot: Metrics: 5xx rate 18% (prev baseline 0.4%), avg 95th latency 1.8s -> 6.2s. NAT Gateway NAT-EAST-2 shows SNAT port exhaustion warnings; conntrack spikes. Affected customers: cs-tenant-17 (high), cs-tenant-04 (medium). Region: us-east-2 private cluster.

network-raj: @oncall-erica thx — early suspicion: ephemeral port exhaustion on transit NATs causing half-open connections and TCP resets, then gateway falls back and returns 504/502. Could also be SG misapply on peering route. I'll join.

sre-lee: I'm pulling logs from the gw pod fleet. Seeing a lot of "upstream reset" and "io timeout" from downstream NAT connections. Example log snippet:

```
[2026-03-15T10:05:12Z] gw-47 tcp_proxy: upstream connection failed: connection reset by peer (errno=104)
[2026-03-15T10:05:13Z] gw-48 http: upstream request timed out after 15s
```

eng-infra-maya: Checked NAT CloudWatch. Rate of new TCP connections surged ~10:03 UTC. NAT metrics: ActiveConnections spiked, PortAllocationFailed count incremented. NAT Gateway showing "PortLimitReached" alarms.

oncall-erica: immediate mitigation options? Can we route affected zone to spare NAT / fallback gateway or throttle concurrency on gateway side?

network-raj: We have a spare transit NAT cluster (nat-spare-3) but it's in a different AZ. We can failover routes on the transit appliance. Risk: short blip during BGP reroute. Recommend quick traffic steering of inference-gateway-egress route to nat-spare-3.

sre-lee: Config to update on transit appliance:

```
# quick route change (conceptual):
set route-map INFERENCE-EGRESS match traffic-class 10 set next-hop nat-spare-3
```

oncall-erica: I'll coordinate route flip. @eng-infra-maya can you validate nat-spare-3 has capacity and no SG blocks?

eng-infra-maya: Verified nat-spare-3 ephemeral pool ok, security groups allow egress to internet and peering. No NAT port alarms. Ready to flip.

customer-success-jordan: Heads-up: cs-tenant-17 is on a production run; they're seeing failures now. I'll open a DM with them and update status page.

oncall-erica: Executing route change now. Rolling to nat-spare-3 in a controlled way (traffic-weight 20% -> 50% -> 100%), watching error rate.

incident-bot: ACTION: route-change started by oncall-erica at 10:09 UTC. Auto-rollback threshold: if 5xx > 12% after 5m.

sre-lee: 10:10: 20% -> 50%.

sre-lee: 10:11: 80%.

sre-lee: 10:12: 100% traffic on nat-spare-3. Monitoring.

prod-monitoring-bot: Post-route change: 5xx dropped to 4.2% within 90s; 95th latency down to 2.1s. NAT port errors decreased.

network-raj: Good sign. That supports port exhaustion root cause. We should also confirm conntrack sizing on transit appliance and adjust ephemeral pool. On hosts we saw conntrack table close to 95% on the transit nodes.

eng-infra-maya: Working on increasing conntrack max and tuning NAT sticky timers. Patch planned: update sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max from 262144 -> 524288, and reduce timeout for TIME_WAIT if safe.

oncall-erica: For immediate safety, throttle new inference sessions: reduce max concurrent requests per gw instance from 120 -> 60. This will slow throughput but prevent rapid port churn.

sre-lee: Applied concurrency throttle to inference-gateway-prod (rolling restart with new config). Verifying now.

prod-monitoring-bot: After throttle + route flip: 5xx at 1.1%, latency stable. Customers still reporting some errors but decreased.

customer-success-jordan: Notified cs-tenant-17 and cs-tenant-04 that we're mitigating; sent interim status: "Partial degradation, mitigation in progress; next update in 30m." They acknowledged.

oncall-erica: Next steps: keep traffic on nat-spare-3 until infra changes deployed, schedule a maintenance window to increase conntrack and add NAT capacity. Postmortem owner: @network-raj. I'll handoff to night oncall in 30m if stable.

network-raj: I'll own postmortem and engineering mitigation. Immediate remediation: add 2x NAT endpoints to the transit pool and roll conntrack changes to transit nodes. Also plan to add metrics and alert for PortAllocationFailed > 0.

eng-infra-maya: Creating infra change: CHG-2026-345: bump conntrack and add NAT endpoints. Target ETA 2 hours for non-disruptive deploy (need to coordinate with routing team).

sre-lee: Quick check: any signs of SG rule misapply? I grepped audit logs; there are no recent SG policy changes in the window. Looks like pure port exhaustion due to burst of connections.

oncall-erica: Great. Summarizing for handoff:
- Incident start: 3077777000 (~10:04 UTC)
- Impact: elevated 5xx/504 for inference-gateway-prod in us-east-2 affecting ~2 tenants
- Root cause (probable): NAT ephemeral port exhaustion + transit conntrack saturation
- Mitigations applied: route flipped to nat-spare-3, concurrency throttle, planned conntrack sysctl and add NAT endpoints
- Postmortem owner: network-raj

oncall-erica: handing off to night coverage. Last check: 5xx at 0.9% and stable for 6m.

incident-bot: NOTE: Oncall handoff from oncall-erica to oncall-jamie scheduled at 10:40 UTC. Please include runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/nat-ephemeral-exhaustion

customer-success-jordan: I'll follow up with affected customers and schedule an RCA call with them once postmortem is ready.

network-raj: filing root-cause ticket and action items. Will include traffic-simulation load test to reproduce and validate new conntrack settings.

oncall-erica: thanks all. Closing active paging. If anything flares, reopen thread.

sre-lee: leaving a short log excerpt for the postmortem:

```
netstat -an | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l
> 124532
sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count
> 248900
```

prod-monitoring-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: error rate back to baseline and no new PortAllocationFailed alarms after remediation. Auto-close in 1h unless reopened.

customer-success-jordan: confirmed customers saw recovery. Marking as "impacted but mitigated" for support tracking. Will push updates to status page.

oncall-erica: thanks team. Follow-ups: CHG-2026-345 rollout, add alert for NAT port failures, add canary for conntrack growth. Good job. :thumbsup!
